entries.clue: Like fruit to be very nice? (6)

blocks.note: a stone fruit plus the -y suffix meaning 'like', read literally

annotation.surface: Someone wondering whether being fruit-like is a compliment.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is whimsical: nobody really uses PEACHY to mean peach-like, but that is what the word's parts say.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in informal speech, as in 'everything's fine and dandy', with a jokey literal sense of resembling a peach alongside.

entries.clue: Marketing look that is plain (7)

blocks.note: an air = a look or manner

annotation.surface: A critique of an advertising style that is dull and unadorned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as an adjective describing the look; it is the noun, a flat grassland.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the North American grasslands are a vast flat plain.

entries.clue: Had meal at home with ultimate casserole in a can (3,2)

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of casserole is taken
'in' places one thing inside another, here the letter inside the phrase for a can

annotation.surface: Someone dining at home on the dregs of a tinned stew.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the tinned casserole the meal; the can is only a container for a single E.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to eat in is the opposite of eating out, so the past tense means had a meal at home.

entries.clue: Someone getting married who needs a lift? (7)

blocks.note: to get hitched = to get married

annotation.surface: A nervous bride or groom in need of cheering up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Needs a lift' pretends to mean a mood boost for the nervous spouse-to-be; it is a car ride. The first sense is whimsical, since nobody really calls a bride a hitcher.
annotation.definitionFit: A jokey coinage from 'getting hitched' for marrying, plus the ordinary short form of hitchhiker for someone thumbing a ride.

entries.clue: Fixed goods in dire condition (6)

indicators.note: 'in' says the goods are placed inside the other letters
to condition something is to work it into a new shape, so the letters of dire are reshaped

blocks.note: G = good, so two goods = GG

annotation.surface: A complaint that merchandise arrived broken and was patched up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goods' looks like merchandise; it is two lots of G for good. 'Fixed' means repaired in the surface and crooked in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The crooked sense of fixed, as in a match or election arranged dishonestly in advance, not the repaired sense the surface uses.

entries.clue: Drinks over half, holding cloth to protect clothes (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'over' means turned upwards, so the letters read in reverse
one piece holds the other in its arms, so the cloth sits inside the reversed half

blocks.note: a bib keeps food off clothes

annotation.surface: A messy drinker spilling half of each glass and needing a bib.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' looks like a noun in the surface; it is the verb. 'Over' is not about spilling but about turning SEMI upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb, slightly formal or jocular, as in someone who has imbibed too freely.

entries.clue: Briefly bear with popular girl’s moaning (9)

indicators.note: cut short, so the bear loses its last letter

blocks.note: GRIZZLY (a bear) minus its last letter
G is an abbreviation for girl

annotation.surface: Advice to put up with a popular girl's constant whining for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' reads as the verb 'put up with'; it is the animal, a grizzly.
annotation.definitionFit: A British regional word for fretful whining, used especially of small children.

entries.clue: Copy model’s vintage jacket (7)

annotation.surface: A fashion model's retro jacket being copied.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk; it is the Model T, Ford's early car and a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by period: the close-fitting jacket men wore from the 14th to 17th centuries is truly vintage.

entries.clue: Build enthusiasm for great little dog on the radio (4,2)

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the words are what they sound like

annotation.surface: A radio presenter talking up a wonderful puppy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great' has to become HIGH, as in great or high ranking, before the sound match appears.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb from publicity: to promote something noisily so that people get excited about it.

entries.clue: Very clear Dad’s temporary home left retired son Victor with debts (8,7)

indicators.note: to retire is to go back or withdraw, so the word for son runs backwards

blocks.note: a tent is a temporary home
V is Victor in the NATO alphabet
IOUs are written promises to pay

annotation.surface: A family saga: Dad living in a tent after his son left home in debt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired' pretends the son has stopped working; it only turns BOY around.
annotation.definitionFit: An intensified synonym: patently means plainly, and the phrase stacks two words for evident to mean very clear.

entries.clue: Upheaval with CERN forced to remove IT (6)

indicators.note: the letters are forced out of their order into a new one
remove means take away, so the letters I and T are taken out of the word before them

annotation.surface: A physics lab ordered to scrap its computer department, causing chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word; it is fodder, and IT is not information technology but the letters I and T.
annotation.definitionFit: The emotional sense: a painful uprooting, as when leaving home is a real upheaval.

entries.clue: Pocket tablets doctor’s brought in and sleep late exhausted (8)

indicators.note: the doctor is brought in between the tablets, placed inside them
exhausted means emptied out, so late loses its middle letters

blocks.note: E = an ecstasy tablet, so two of them
zz = the snoring sound of sleep

annotation.surface: A doctor prescribing pills and then oversleeping, worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to take for yourself. 'Tablets' are the drug-slang E, not medicine.
annotation.definitionFit: Pocket as a verb means to take money dishonestly for yourself, which is what a clerk skimming funds entrusted to them does.

entries.clue: Calm down as gate undone with hairpin (3,1,4)

indicators.note: something undone has come apart, so the letters of gate are put back in another order

blocks.note: a grip or hairgrip is a British name for a bobby pin

annotation.surface: Someone told to relax after picking a gate lock with a hairpin.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a lock being picked; a hairpin is simply a GRIP.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom, usually an impatient command, telling someone to pull themselves together and stop panicking.

entries.clue: Often in the past make up used lead (1,4,4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means the word reads upwards, in reverse
something used has been worked over, so the letters of lead are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: do = make, as in do a sketch

annotation.surface: A vague memory of often making up with a used pencil lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make up' looks like a single phrasal verb; it splits into DO and a direction. 'Used' is an unusual signal for rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase meaning a lot or frequently, as in 'I see him quite a bit'.

entries.clue: Strain admitting husband’s variable and untrustworthy (6)

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the strainer lets the husband inside it

annotation.surface: A strained marriage in which the husband is fickle and not to be trusted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strain' reads as tension in the marriage; it is the kitchen verb, to sieve.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone with evasive, darting looks seems dishonest and not to be trusted.

entries.clue: Happy mojo you seek’s within (6)

indicators.note: within means inside, so the answer lies inside the words that precede it

blocks.note: runs from the end of mojo, through you, into the start of seek's

annotation.surface: A self-help slogan: the happy mojo you seek is inside you.
annotation.walkthrough: The self-help line tells you exactly where to look: the answer is within the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, a little more elevated than glad, meaning full of joy.

entries.clue: Cover rampant body odour with brand of deodorant Charlie’s wearing (7)

indicators.note: running wild, so the two letters are out of their order
the brand wears the letter like a garment, so it goes inside

blocks.note: Sure is a British deodorant brand
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Charlie masking a bad smell with a spray of deodorant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' reads as masking the smell and is still the definition, now as a verb meaning to hide from view.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to block something from sight, as clouds hide the sun.

entries.clue: Old sailors each taking pet aboard ship (7)

indicators.note: on board the ship, and since the ship is SS the letters go inside S…S

annotation.surface: Veteran sailors each bringing a pet on board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aboard ship' is standard crosswordese for going inside SS.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a seasoned veteran mariner, usually with 'old' in front.

entries.clue: Mostly ignore false prophet’s dividing faith (8)

indicators.note: most of the word but not all, so ignore drops its last letter
false means not genuine, so the letters are put in a false order
the prophet splits the rearranged letters, sitting between them

blocks.note: Eli is a priest and prophet in the Old Testament

annotation.surface: Advice to disregard a false prophet who splits a religious community.
annotation.walkthrough: 'False prophet' reads as one phrase; 'false' belongs to IGNOR and the prophet is plain ELI.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a faith is a system of belief, as in the Christian or Muslim faith.

entries.clue: Occasionally urged on team live (6)

indicators.note: only now and then, so just every other letter of urged is used

annotation.surface: A fan sometimes cheering on the team at a live match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Urged on' looks like a phrase; 'on' just joins the pieces. 'Live' is the verb, not the adjective of a live match.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain, slightly formal synonym for the verb live, meaning to have your home somewhere.

entries.clue: Spill a keg ale that’s lively (7)

indicators.note: the letters jump about into a new order

annotation.surface: A pub order: spill some of that fizzy keg beer.
annotation.walkthrough: Keg ale is lively because it is carbonated, which disguises the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Spill as a noun: an escape of liquid from its container.

entries.clue: Late with extra owing (7)

annotation.surface: A late payment with an extra charge still owing.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a late-payment notice, which is where the answer itself belongs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a library book or a bill past its deadline is late.

entries.clue: American drift-raced with special old vehicles (4,4)

indicators.note: letters that drift wander out of place

annotation.surface: An American drift-racing old cars in a special event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drift-raced' reads as one motorsport term; the hyphen hides that 'drift' is the signal and RACED the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: second-hand motors on a dealer's forecourt are old vehicles.

entries.clue: Jobs creation finally bears fruit (6)

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so take the final letter of bears

annotation.surface: A job-creation scheme at last paying off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jobs creation' reads as employment policy; it is Steve Jobs and his company. 'Bears fruit' is a phrase, but 'bears' only supplies its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the commonest orchard crop is a type of fruit, so the plural fits 'fruit' used collectively.

entries.clue: Beginning to rein in worthless agent (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the start of rein is used
'in' places the letter inside the word for worthless

blocks.note: poxy is British slang for rubbish, worthless

annotation.surface: A boss starting to rein in a useless employee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worthless agent' reads as one phrase; the agent is the definition and 'worthless' the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone authorised to act or vote on another's behalf is their agent.

entries.clue: One of four in the pack – she-cat with main food gone – drops, disheartened (5,2,8)

definitions.text: One of four in the pack

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged
losing its heart, drops keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: a queen is a female cat

annotation.surface: A cat whose food has vanished and who has lost heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pack' suggests a pack of animals beside the she-cat; it is a pack of cards, which has four queens.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a standard deck holds four queens, one per suit, and this is the red one with the lozenge suit.

entries.clue: Join line travelling with holy woman (6)

indicators.note: the letters travel away from their places into a new order

annotation.surface: A nun joining a queue on a journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like a queue to join; it is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Join in the sense of signing up, especially for the armed forces.

entries.clue: Again, key’s required to start old Jaguar (2-4)

indicators.note: the letter that starts a word is its first, so only the opening of required is used

blocks.note: the E-Type, a classic 1960s Jaguar sports car

annotation.surface: A classic car owner once more needing the ignition key.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as a car key; it is the verb, to type on a keyboard. 'Again, key' together means key in once more.
annotation.definitionFit: Key as a verb means enter on a keyboard, and doing it again is a repeat of that typing.
